confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for food and drink prices. The food and drink sources were mostly crowd-sourced or modelled cost-of-living sites (MyLifeElsewhere, CityCost, Expatistan, travel guides), and some were undated. I found no authoritative current survey of Siem Reap prices. Coffee, beer and meals are reasonably supported, and mid-range meal prices vary widely by venue. Cocktail and wine rest on thin, mixed evidence: sources gave about $5-12 for cocktails and about $4-5 for house wine, and one happy-hour listing showed $3.50 cocktails. I set both at the low end of tourist-area prices, relative to local beer at about $1.50. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge for a typical low-season Siem Reap tourist market. I did not search for or inspect any accommodation prices or listings. Because Cambodia is heavily dollarised, I treated prices as USD.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are based on the Siem Reap search results, with Cambodia-wide figures used as a cross-check. They fit the low-cost Mekong-region tourist pattern seen in Phnom Penh and other tourist towns in Cambodia and Laos, with Siem Reap slightly cheaper than Phnom Penh.
